name: Glowforge Aura
tagline: Consumer-friendly diode craft laser with the simplest setup
tldr: Glowforge's compact 6W diode Craft Laser for crafters. Easy software, autofocus, quick setup and a Passthrough slot for long projects, but cutting is limited to thin materials. The catch: a cloud-based app (optional Premium subscription from $20/mo) and far less power than CO₂ machines like the xTool P2S.

priceRange.note: Official Glowforge store, Oct 2026: $999 (list price $1,199); optional Premium subscription from $20/mo

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Enclosed craft laser with autofocus and Passthrough for long projects
Integrated cabinet helps contain the beam and everyday smoke versus open-frame diodes
Software listed on the profile: test your workflow (LightBurn or maker app) on scrap first
cons: Venting outside or a filter is still required, like any laser cutter
Cutting is limited to thin materials: 1/4 in (6 mm) max according to Glowforge
beginnerNotes: This profile covers Glowforge Aura. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks before buying, then compare nearby models on the Compare page.
proTips: If you take the optional Premium subscription, factor it over 2–3 years into your budget. Proofgrade materials are convenient but expensive: third-party plywood works with testing. Aura is craft-scale, not sign-shop scale.
primaryUse: Simple diode laser cutting and engraving for crafters who prioritize ease of use over power and cost efficiency.
mainObjective: Easiest laser setup for crafters who want zero tinkering

editorialDepth.advantages: Glowforge Aura is built for crafters: paper, card, thin wood, leather and engraving, with autofocus and a Passthrough slot for long pieces. Its 6W diode keeps it compact but limits cutting to thin stock.
editorialDepth.limitations: Avoid for thick wood or acrylic, sign-shop volume, or offline use. Bare metal marking stays out of scope.
